graph.title: Burning the bootloader: ATmega328P on a breadboard programmed by an Arduino as ISP
notes: Built the first diagram (burning the bootloader with Arduino as ISP). The second diagram (USB-serial upload with the microcontroller removed from the Arduino) and the minimal no-crystal variant are not included.

Wiring: Arduino pin 10 -> ATmega RESET (pin 1), 11 -> MOSI (pin 17), 12 -> MISO (pin 18), 13 -> SCK (pin 19). 5V and GND go to the breadboard rails; VCC (7), AVCC (20) to + rail; GND (8, 22) to - rail.

The 10k pull-up resistor goes from RESET (pin 1) to the + rail. The crystal sits across pins 9 and 10, each with a 22 pF capacitor to ground. The resistor value is set to 10000 even though the catalogue entry is labelled 100 ohm.
Chip orientation: pins 1-14 in the lower bank (row f, columns 5-18), pins 15-28 in the upper bank (row e, columns 18-5). Breadboard hole positions and rail indices are estimated from the picture.

The manual lists 10 jumper wires. The picture shows only some of the power wires, so I used 12 to give every chip power and ground pin a route (AVCC and the second GND included). The two blue on-board wires in the picture are assumed to be the crystal connections, which I made with the crystal legs directly.

breadboard.name: Solderless breadboard
breadboard.port_rule: Holes are named '<column><bank>.<row>': column 1-30, bank 't' (top half, rows a-e) or 'b' (bottom half, rows f-j), e.g. '12t.c', '7b.h'. The 5 holes of one column-bank are one strip. Power rails: 'tp.<n>', 'tn.<n>', 'bp.<n>', 'bn.<n>' (each rail is one strip).
